summary: Adds three endpoints: a user search by name, a per-key request counter guarded by a mutex, and an upstream status check. The change also registers all three in main.go.

findings.title: Search query built from the name parameter
findings.problem: Search pastes the name query parameter into the SQL text with fmt.Sprintf. The value is not escaped or bound.
findings.consequence: Any caller of GET /users can inject SQL and read or change any data the database user can reach.
findings.fix: Pass name to QueryContext as a bound parameter. Remove the Sprintf call.
findings.suggested_change: rows, err := h.DB.QueryContext(r.Context(), "SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE name = ?", name)

findings.title: Mutex stays locked when the key is missing
findings.problem: Count locks h.mu and then returns early on an empty key without unlocking it.
findings.consequence: One request without a key leaves the mutex held forever. Every later GET /count request then blocks indefinitely.
findings.fix: Check the key before taking the lock, or unlock with defer right after Lock.

findings.title: Response body closed before the error check
findings.problem: fetchStatus defers resp.Body.Close before checking err. When http.Get fails, resp is nil and evaluating resp.Body panics.
findings.consequence: Whenever the upstream is unreachable, Upstream panics instead of answering 502. The client sees a dropped connection.
findings.fix: Move the defer below the error check.

findings.title: New endpoints have no tests
findings.problem: The change adds Search, Count and Upstream, but the repository has no test files. No test exercises these endpoints.
findings.consequence: Bugs like the leaked lock and the nil response panic reach production unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add handler tests that cover a missing key, a failed upstream fetch and a search by name.

dropped.reason: This hit flags the same Sprintf query that the c1 finding already reports.
